messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — after the kernel-selector change to `auto` on the qwen2.5 runtime we landed last night, we’re seeing a regression on p99 latency for mixed-lang traffic (en + CJK). Numbers: +15% p99, +9% median on dedicated-small. Repro steps below.

Priya Nair: ugh. do we have a trace or flame? which path does `auto` pick for these requests?

Alex Chen: quick profiling attached inline: ran `./tools/infer_profiler --model qwen2.5 --seq 2048 --batch-mix 8,2 --kernel-selector auto` on a single pod. Noticed heavy time in attention kernel switch and an extra memcpy before KV write. Paste:

```
# simplified perf summary (ns/op)
attention_fused:  12000
attention_split:   8500
kv_write_memcpy:    4300
kv_commit:          1100
other:              2200
```

Samir Patel: that `kv_write_memcpy` is suspicious — looks like an extra copy/transpose on the autokernel path. Could be because autokernel assumes KV head layout=Hk, but our tokenizer->head mapping for CJK uses a different byte stride.

Taylor G.: also saw increased kvcache churn in the same window — eviction counts up by ~30% when batches mix short en prompts with long cjk. Could be batching heuristic incorrectly merging streams which then forces small-prefix KV invalidation.

Priya Nair: can you paste the runtime config you used? esp: `rope_scale`, `kv_layout` and `batching.mode`?

Alex Chen: config snip:

```
model: qwen2.5
kernel_selector: auto
rope_scale: 0.98
kv_layout: [heads, dim]  # runtime sees HxD
batching:
  mode: mixed
  max_seq: 2048
  pad_to_max: false
  adaptive_window: 128
```

Alex Chen: note: when I force `kernel_selector: fused_attention_v1` the memcpy disappears and p99 drops back to baseline. So root cause likely in kernel code path assumptions about kv layout and RoPE precomputation ordering.

Samir Patel: hypothesis: `auto` chooses a vectorized attention that expects RoPE applied differently (pre vs post transpose) which changes memory layout for KV buffers, then runtime does a defensive memcpy to a canonical layout before committing to the global KV cache. That explains both memcpy and extra eviction because canonicalization changes pointer/equality.

Priya Nair: good hypothesis. can you bisect which commit in the kernel switch introduced the canonicalization? maybe a change in kernel API when adding ALiBi hybrid support.

Alex Chen: starting bisect now. quick command I ran to reproduce perf trace: `./tools/bench_infer --model qwen2.5 --kernel auto --seq 2048 --batch 10 --langmix en,cjk --profile=full > ./out/prof.txt` — attaching the interesting snippet here.

Infra Bot: Deploy monitor: pod/rwi-infer-12 restarted at 2312345605 due to OOM during the same test (not sure correlated).

Taylor G.: OOM could be because memcpy increases peak memory transiently; for 2048 seq + big batch that pushes GPU over. worth running with `pad_to_max: true` to keep allocations stable and see if memcpy still happens.

Samir Patel: quick experiment suggestion: add a shim in runtime near KV commit to skip canonical-copy when `kv_layout` metadata matches the kernel's expected layout. If that fixes perf, we can add small conservative check instead of heavy memcpy. Also test with `rope_scale: 1.0` vs `0.98` — RoPE interp rounding can change where we keep cached cos/sin and may change memory layout timing.

Priya Nair: can someone run a trimmed repro: `--batch 4 --seq 1024` and `--batch 12 --seq 256` to see whether long-seq vs many-short is the main trigger? I'll own the bisect if Alex confirms repro script.

Alex Chen: will run both now and post numbers in ~20m. early note: `--batch 4 --seq 1024` still shows ~9% p99 uplift; `--batch 12 --seq 256` shows ~18% (so mixed short-many seems worse).

Taylor G.: action items: 1) Alex to push repro artifacts and raw profiler output, 2) Samir to prototype layout-check shim, 3) Priya to bisect kernel-selector merge commits, 4) Ops to run limited canary pin to `fused_attention_v1` for one worker pool.

Samir Patel: small workaround we can roll now: set `kernel_selector: fused_attention_v1` for CJK-heavy routes and set `batching.pad_to_max: true` for dedicated-small until we have a proper patch.

Alex Chen: thanks — posting profiler logs and perf flame link: https://internal.redwood/profiles/2312345678/flame.html (internal). Will update when bisect narrows it down. :eyes:
